original_question: Let p be a prime. Let G be a transitive subgroup of the group of finitary permutations F Sym(Ω) of a set Ω, let N be a normal subgroup of G, and let S be a transitive Sylow p-subgroup of G. (a) Is it true that S ∩ N is a Sylow p-subgroup of N? (b) Is it true that SN/N is a Sylow p-subgroup of G/N? (c) Are any two transitive Sylow p-subgroups of G locally conjugate in G? Two subgroups X, Y of a group G are said to be locally conjugate if there is a locally inner automorphism φ of G such that X φ = Y. An automorphism φ of G is said to be locally inner if for every finite subset A ⊆ G there is an element g = g(A) ∈ G such that aφ = g −1 ag for all a ∈ A.
target_in_paper: Section 21, Problem 21.5 (A. O. Asar), page 162: the three-part open problem about transitive Sylow p-subgroups of transitive subgroups of FSym(Ω). ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper extremely closely: it has the correct ambient group G <= FSym(Ω), the assumptions that G is transitive on Ω and N is normal in G, the hypothesis that S is a transitive Sylow p-subgroup of G, all three subquestions (a)-(c), and the paper's definitions of 'locally conjugate' and 'locally inner'. In substance, it is almost verbatim Problem 21.5. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: For a fully stand-alone formulation, it helps to make explicit that since G is a subgroup of the finitary symmetric group, G is locally finite, so 'Sylow p-subgroup' is being used in the infinite-group/local-finite sense (that is, a maximal p-subgroup). This is implicit in the notebook's setting rather than separately stated in Problem 21.5. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let p be a prime, let Ω be a set, and let G be a transitive subgroup of the finitary symmetric group FSym(Ω). Let N be a normal subgroup of G, and let S be a transitive Sylow p-subgroup of G (with 'Sylow p-subgroup' understood in the locally finite sense). Must the following hold: (i) S ∩ N is a Sylow p-subgroup of N; (ii) SN/N is a Sylow p-subgroup of G/N; and (iii) any two transitive Sylow p-subgroups of G are locally conjugate in G, meaning that for any such subgroups X and Y there exists a locally inner automorphism φ of G carrying X to Y, where φ is locally inner if for every finite subset A of G there exists g(A) in G such that φ(a) = g(A)^(-1) a g(A) for all a in A?
justification: arXiv:1401.0300 is the Kourovka Notebook, and the draft is not merely inspired by the paper: it is essentially the exact wording of Problem 21.5 in Section 21 on page 162. So the right refinement is a very light cleanup into a single self-contained research question, not a broader reformulation. The neighboring Problem 21.6 is a different question about the cyclic-block property and should not be merged into this one. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300))
